system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are internal funnel decay, and only the onboarding lever sits upstream of both, so it has the best claim on sustainable qualified revenue rather than a one-quarter defensive response. The competitor's entry pricing is real, but memory_73's promotional-pricing result is the weakest fit for the stated objective: it reports acquisition and revenue lift with no evidence about the durability or quality of the accounts acquired, and discount-led matching of an aggressive entrant tends to import price-sensitive, low-retention revenue while resetting our own price expectations. That is a downstream-value risk I am explicitly declining to take on the only slot available. I am spending verification on the two memories my chosen action actually rests on rather than on the option I am rejecting. memory_86 is the load-bearing claim, and its stated outcomes (completion rates, time-to-value, early adoption) are all proxies measured near the top of the funnel; I need the source record to see whether any downstream retention or qualified-revenue measurement existed, and how far past week one it ran, before I assume a completion lift converts to durable revenue. memory_31 is the mechanism I would most likely reach for (cutting required signup fields), and it carries a specific hazard the consolidated summary cannot see: removing qualification fields can raise activation while degrading lead quality and sales routing, which would look like a win on the metric I am chasing and a loss on the objective I am serving. It is also 64 days old and predates whatever changed this quarter. If the archive shows either result was proxy-only or field-reduction harmed qualification, I will keep the onboarding slot but restrict the change to sequencing and step-count rather than deleting qualification data, and instrument retention and downstream qualified revenue as primary rather than secondary. memory_91 is my fallback within the same activation problem if onboarding evidence collapses, since in-product messaging touches activation without altering what we collect at signup. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the inherited evidence supports the direction but not the magnitude at the funnel depth I care about, and the current declines mean the baseline these memories were measured against no longer holds. I want a guardrail on qualified-lead quality and week-four retention with a pre-committed stop, so a null or negative downstream result is legible instead of being masked by a completion-rate win.
